column2: All commanded observances serve life, multiplication, entry and inheritance of the sworn land; every stated purpose remains.
The remembered wilderness journey afflicts, tests and reveals the heart's obedience or disobedience. No forty-year phrase is imported into this selected unit.
Affliction, hunger and manna unknown to the fathers teach dependence on every word through God's mouth, with man shall live repeated.
Unworn garments and uncalloused feet persist forty years; the selected calloused sense is not changed to swollen.
The Lord's chastening is compared with a man's chastening his son, retaining the educational family image.
Keeping commandments involves walking His ways and fearing Him; both responses remain.
The good spacious land has torrents and deep springs flowing through plains and hills, preserving both water forms and terrains.
Wheat, barley, vines, figs, pomegranates, olive oil and honey remain in the abundance list.
Bread without poverty and no lack accompany iron stones and mined copper; selected material references are retained without modern extraction details.
Eating and fullness precede blessing the Lord in relation to the good land He gave.
column3: Upon the good land retains a possible locative reading of epi; whether for the good land better expresses the blessing's ground needs further syntactic review.

column2: Forgetting the Lord is linked with failure to keep commandments, judgments and ordinances; all categories remain.
Fullness and good houses introduce the prosperity condition continued into the next clauses.
Herds, flocks, silver, gold and all possessions multiply; the deliberate repeated multiplication remains.
An elevated heart risks forgetting the deliverer from Egypt and bondage; the inward pride image remains.
Biting serpents, scorpions, thirst and lack of water contrast with a spring from sheer rock. Generic Greek animal singulars are naturally collective plurals here, not counted individuals.
Manna unknown to the fathers serves affliction, testing and eventual good in their latter days; all three purposes remain.
The forbidden inward boast attributes great wealth to personal strength and hand-power; wealth is contextual to the preceding possessions.
The Lord gives strength to gain wealth in establishing the ancestral covenant; the source of capacity remains distinct from its product.
Utter forgetting, following other gods, service and worship bring the witnessed warning of destruction; heaven and earth are explicit witnesses in the selected text.
Israel faces the same destruction as other nations because it did not hear the Lord's voice; the causal conclusion remains.
Today's crossing seeks inheritance against greater nations and heaven-high walled cities, preserving both obstacles.
The Anakites are great, numerous and tall, with the remembered question about who can resist them retained.
The Lord advances as consuming fire, destroys and turns back enemies; Israel's subsequent destruction of them remains a distinct action.
The rejected boast concerns plural righteous deeds; the stated contrasting reason is the nations' ungodliness.
Neither Israel's righteousness nor holiness of heart explains entry; the nations' ungodliness and covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob do.
The denial of righteous deeds as cause repeats, with stiff-neckedness as the stated reason.
Remember and do not forget both remain, recalling continuous disobedience from Egypt until the present place.
Horeb's provocation and the Lord's destructive anger introduce the calf recollection.
Moses ascends for covenant tablets and stays forty days and nights without bread or water; both duration and fasting are explicit.
Two stone tablets bear all words written by God's finger, spoken on the assembly day; the selected wording does not add a fire phrase here.
The forty days and nights and two covenant tablets are deliberately repeated.
Your people and whom you brought out address Moses; their speedy departure is from the way you commanded, preserving the selected human addressee.
The selected once and twice speech introduction remains before the stiff-necked assessment.
Destruction and removal of the name are contrasted with making Moses a great, strong and more numerous nation.
Moses descends while the mountain burns, with two tablets in two hands; both repetitions remain.
Sin, a molten image and departure from the commanded way are all seen; no unexpressed calf noun is inserted here.
Both tablets are seized, thrown from both hands and broken before Israel, retaining the staged actions.
The second entreaty lasts forty days and nights with no bread or water over all the people's sins; the selected entreaty is not changed to a bodily prostration.
Present I am afraid remains amid the narrated wrath and fury, followed by the Lord's hearing at this time also.
Aaron is specifically threatened by intense anger, and Moses prays for him also; both additions to the people's case remain.
The calf is called your sin, then burned, broken, finely ground and cast as dust into the descending torrent; each action remains.
Burning, Testing and Graves of Desire are translated selected place names, preserving their descriptive meaning.
At Kadesh-barnea, disobedience is joined by two explicit negatives: not believing Him and not hearing His voice.
Disobedience dates from when He became known to you in the selected passive construction, not from when Moses knew them.
Forty-day-and-night entreaty is repeated and explained by the announced destruction; the apparent repetition is retained.
Lord, Lord, King of the gods and both great-strength clauses remain, together with mighty hand and uplifted arm. Direct address retains Thou and Thy/Thine.
Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are remembered as servants under the oath by Thyself; hardness, ungodliness and sins are all named in the plea.
The feared foreign accusation combines inability and hatred as reasons for wilderness slaughter; it remains a quotation within prayer, not the narrator's assertion.
The people and inheritance are reaffirmed with Egyptian deliverance by great strength and uplifted arm, retaining the repeated prayer grounds.
Two replacement stone tablets like the first and a wooden ark are commanded before ascent.
The Lord writes the former words on the new tablets, and Moses places them in the ark; writing and placement have distinct agents.
Decay-resistant wood renders the selected descriptive material without importing a botanical identification; two tablets are hewn and carried up.
The ten words match the first writing and the mountain speech from fire; the Lord gives the tablets to Moses.
Moses descends and places the tablets in his ark, where they remain as commanded.
Beeroth of Iakim's sons leads to Misadai, where Aaron dies and is buried and Eleazar succeeds; the selected route is not harmonized with Numbers.
Misadai's continuation goes to Gadgad then Jotbathah, with the latter's flowing-water terrain retained.
Levi is set apart to carry the ark, stand and minister before the Lord, and bless in His name until today.
Levites have no territorial share, and the selected singular his inheritance and unto him remain after the plural opening.
column3: The singular reference to Levi following plural Levites needs explicit reader consideration; this pass does not smooth it into unmarked plural pronouns.

column2: Forty days and nights and the Lord's renewed hearing precede His refusal to destroy Israel, preserving both acts.
Moses goes before the people so they enter and inherit the land sworn to their fathers.
Fear, walking all ways, love and wholehearted service remain in the question about the Lord's requirement.
Keeping commandments and ordinances completes that question with welfare as its purpose.
Heaven, heaven of heaven, earth and everything in it belong to the Lord, retaining the selected singular nested heaven expression.
Preference, love and choice concern the fathers and their descendants identified as you, above all nations today.
Circumcising hardness of heart and no longer stiffening the neck preserve both selected bodily metaphors.
Propose fearsome for fearful so the adjective clearly means causing fear rather than being afraid. God of gods, Lord of lords, greatness, might, impartiality and refusal of bribes remain.
Justice includes sojourner, orphan and widow, followed by love expressed in bread and clothing for the sojourner; the selected first sojourner mention remains.
Love for the sojourner is grounded in Israel's own sojourning in Egypt, preserving the repeated noun.
Fear, service, attachment and oath by His name all remain, matching the selected fourfold instruction.
The Lord is Israel's boast and God, whose great and glorious deeds were seen; selected glorious is not replaced by fearsome.
Seventy souls went down to Egypt in this selected passage, and the present multitude is compared to heaven's stars; seventy is not harmonized with Genesis' different count.
